```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

## Goal

Predict the total point differential × total steals across 7 NBA games, using team box-score
statistics from recent games.

The original version of this project (a class prediction competition) let the model use
point differential, steals and the final scores as predictors. Those are the pieces the
response is built from, so the model looked very accurate but could not truly forecast a game
that hasn't happened yet. This version removes them, compares several models on a held-out
test set, and makes the forecast with a model that only uses ordinary box-score stats.

```{r libraries}
library(tidyverse)
library(randomForest)
library(knitr)
```

## Data

Both files should sit in the same folder as this file (sources listed at the end).

```{r load-data}
scores <- read_csv("TeamStatistics.csv")
steals <- read_csv("team_traditional.csv")
```

```{r clean}
# Keep only the 14 teams playing in the 7 games being predicted
teams   <- c("Magic", "Knicks", "Celtics", "Raptors", "Nuggets", "Hornets", "Trail Blazers",
             "Grizzlies", "Warriors", "Bulls", "Lakers", "76ers", "Thunder", "Jazz")
abbrevs <- c("ORL", "NYK", "BOS", "TOR", "DEN", "CHA", "POR",
             "MEM", "GSW", "CHI", "LAL", "PHI", "OKC", "UTA")

scores2 <- scores %>%
  filter(teamName %in% teams)

steals2 <- steals %>%
  filter(home %in% abbrevs) %>%
  rename(gameId = gameid) %>%            # match the ID name in the scores data
  filter(date >= as.Date("2025-01-01"))  # recent games only

# Join on game ID, then keep one row per game
# (each game appears twice, once from each team's side)
games <- scores2 %>%
  inner_join(steals2, by = "gameId") %>%
  distinct(gameId, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(points_diff = abs(teamScore - opponentScore),
         y = points_diff * steals)

nrow(games)
```

## Predictors

`y` is built from point differential and steals, so any column that contains those numbers
(or the final scores) would let the model "see" part of the answer. Those columns are excluded.

```{r predictors}
box_preds <- c("FGM", "FGA", "FG%", "3PM", "3PA", "3P%", "FTM", "FTA", "FT%",
               "OREB", "DREB", "REB", "AST", "TOV", "BLK", "PF")
leaky     <- c("points_diff", "STL", "teamScore", "opponentScore", "+/-")

model_data <- games %>%
  select(teamName, all_of(box_preds), all_of(leaky), y) %>%
  drop_na()

summary(model_data$y)
```

## Exploratory data analysis

```{r eda}
ggplot(model_data, aes(x = y)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Point Differential × Steals per Game",
       x = "Point differential × steals", y = "Games") +
  theme_minimal()

# Correlation of each box-score stat with y
model_data %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(box_preds), ~ cor(.x, y))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Stat", values_to = "Correlation") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(Stat, Correlation), y = Correlation)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Correlation with Point Differential × Steals", x = "Stat", y = "Correlation") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Train/test split

```{r split}
set.seed(455)
train_rows <- sample(nrow(model_data), size = floor(0.7 * nrow(model_data)))
train <- model_data[train_rows, ]
test  <- model_data[-train_rows, ]
```

## Models

```{r models}
box_formula <- reformulate(sprintf("`%s`", box_preds), "y")

# 1. Empty model: predicts the training average for every game
empty_pred <- rep(mean(train$y), nrow(test))

# 2. Original class model, for reference only: it uses point differential, steals and the
#    final scores, which are part of the response
original_model <- lm(y ~ points_diff + STL + TOV + teamScore + opponentScore +
                       AST + PF + `FT%` + BLK, data = train)
original_pred <- predict(original_model, newdata = test)

# 3. Stepwise regression using box-score stats only
full  <- lm(box_formula, data = train)
empty <- lm(y ~ 1, data = train)
step_model <- step(empty, scope = list(upper = full), direction = "both", trace = 0)
formula(step_model)
step_pred <- predict(step_model, newdata = test)

# 4. Same predictors with a square-root transformation on y
#    (y is right-skewed, as the histogram shows)
sqrt_formula <- update(formula(step_model), sqrt(y) ~ .)
sqrt_model <- lm(sqrt_formula, data = train)
sqrt_pred <- predict(sqrt_model, newdata = test)^2   # square to undo the transformation

# 5. Random forest using all box-score stats
set.seed(455)
rf_model <- randomForest(x = train[, box_preds], y = train$y, importance = TRUE)
rf_pred <- predict(rf_model, newdata = test[, box_preds])
```

## Comparing models on the test set

RMSE is how far off the predictions are, on average, in the units of y. Lower is better.

```{r rmse}
rmse <- function(actual, predicted) sqrt(mean((actual - predicted)^2))

results <- tibble(
  Model = c("Empty (training average)",
            "Original class model (uses parts of the answer)",
            "Stepwise, box-score stats",
            "Stepwise, square root of y",
            "Random forest, box-score stats"),
  Forecastable = c("Yes", "No", "Yes", "Yes", "Yes"),
  RMSE = c(rmse(test$y, empty_pred),
           rmse(test$y, original_pred),
           rmse(test$y, step_pred),
           rmse(test$y, sqrt_pred),
           rmse(test$y, rf_pred))
) %>%
  arrange(RMSE)

kable(results, digits = 2)
```

```{r rmse-plot}
ggplot(results, aes(x = reorder(Model, -RMSE), y = RMSE,
                    fill = Forecastable)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Yes" = "steelblue", "No" = "grey60")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Test RMSE", title = "Test RMSE by Model") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Diagnostics for the regression models

```{r diagnostics}
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(step_model, which = 1:2, main = "Stepwise")
plot(sqrt_model, which = 1:2, main = "Square root of y")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

## Variable importance (random forest)

```{r importance}
tibble(Stat = rownames(importance(rf_model)),
       Importance = importance(rf_model)[, "%IncMSE"]) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(Stat, Importance), y = Importance)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Random Forest Variable Importance", x = "Stat", y = "% Increase in MSE") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Forecast for the 7 games

The forecast uses the forecastable model with the lowest test RMSE. For each of the 7 home
teams, the model is given that team's average box-score stats.

```{r forecast}
forecastable <- results %>% filter(Forecastable == "Yes")
best_model <- forecastable$Model[1]
best_model

predict_best <- function(newdata) {
  switch(best_model,
         "Empty (training average)"       = rep(mean(train$y), nrow(newdata)),
         "Stepwise, box-score stats"      = predict(step_model, newdata = newdata),
         "Stepwise, square root of y"     = predict(sqrt_model, newdata = newdata)^2,
         "Random forest, box-score stats" = predict(rf_model, newdata = newdata[, box_preds]))
}

# Average box-score stats for each team
team_avgs <- model_data %>%
  group_by(teamName) %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(box_preds), mean))

home_teams <- tibble(teamName = c("Knicks", "Raptors", "Hornets", "Grizzlies",
                                  "Bulls", "76ers", "Jazz"))

forecast_data <- home_teams %>%
  left_join(team_avgs, by = "teamName")

game_preds <- predict_best(forecast_data)
kable(tibble(Home_team = home_teams$teamName, Predicted_y = game_preds), digits = 1)

# The target is (total point differential) × (total steals) across all 7 games.
# Summing 7 per-game products and multiplying by 7 approximates that when games are similar.
final_pred <- sum(game_preds) * 7
final_pred
```

## Sanity check

```{r sanity-check}
avg_diff   <- mean(model_data$points_diff)
avg_steals <- mean(model_data$STL)
(7 * avg_diff) * (7 * avg_steals)
```
